title: "12. Hierarchical analysis masks"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{12. Hierarchical analysis masks}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Event setup supplies the selected group context to `event_masks_server()`.
The analyst chooses a Stream and explicitly starts creation. Pending edits block
dispatch. `store$mask_request()` pins current study, collection and group revisions;
`prepare_masks()` allocates a unique path under the study's mask staging folder.
`launch_event_masks()` calls `write_event_masks` in fluvgeo in a separate process.

The backend owns geometry validation, grid snapping, strict cell-center membership,
parent intersection, compressed disk-backed writing, resource admission and
reopening/hash verification. Centers on exterior or hole edges are excluded;
narrow polygons can have zero included centers. Every saved Reach in the selected
Stream must have a polygon. Missing Reach geometry blocks creation rather than
silently omitting a hierarchy level. Source DEMs and vertical references are not
modified or needed to build the analysis domain.

The default family cap is 50 million cells, with no raster wider than 65,536
columns. Blocks have at most 65,536 centers. Disk admission requires four times
the uncompressed mask payload plus 256 MiB; it does not reserve space. Limits
are conservative safeguards for this first processing increment, not performance
qualification for a full-size analyst study.

The writer creates `verified.json` last. The app checks that saved revisions and
input hashes still match before `publish_masks()` renames the staging directory
into `event-masks/editions`. Cancellation stops and joins the worker; failures,
timeouts, context changes and pending edits leave staging unpublished. Previous
editions remain unchanged. The result shows the edition path and included-cell
counts. Reopening the app clears this session result; editions remain on disk.
An edition browser is not yet provided. Backend `read_event_masks()` reopens and
verifies a saved family for later processing; future mosaics must also confirm
that the edition inputs remain current.

Trace app code in `R/event_masks.R`, `R/survey_event_settings.R` and
`R/study_store.R`; orchestration and publication tests are in
`tests/testthat/test-event-masks.R`. Scientific tests live in sibling fluvgeo's
`tests/testthat/test_event_masks.R`, with the exact contract in
`dev/schemas/event-masks.md`. Grid preflight and masks share the backend's
`.fg_event_grid_inputs()` validation and `.fg_dem_grid_plan()` snapping.

The block I/O follows [terra's read/write API](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/readwrite.html);
center membership uses [sf's geometric predicates](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/reference/geos_binary_pred.html).
Installed-version behavior is covered by synthetic raster tests, including holes,
exact-edge centers, narrow polygons, cropped children and corrupt output.
